- game actions run in one step (rule actions and scripts together): 4,096. To fix: fewer rules firing every step; use every= on rules; check for a rule that raises its own event.
- depth of a chain of events raising events: 8. To fix: break the loop: an emit that another rule answers with an emit of the first.
- kinds in one game; rules in one game: 64; 256. To fix: share a kind and tell things apart with tags and props; merge rules with expressions.
- game.script nodes; source size of one: 16; 64 KiB. To fix: merge scripts; keep data in game.var or state, not in source.
- work one script handler may do in one call (interrupt polls, about 10,000 operations each): 2,000 polls. To fix: the step fails with "a script used up its work budget" and rolls back; loop less per tick, spread work over ticks, or find() once.
- UI elements shown at once: 256. To fix: remove elements you no longer show (ui.remove); build rows with ui.stack.
- worker scripts (the script.js node and the script tool): count, source size, and one frame's time: 16; 64 KiB; 250 ms. To fix: a frame over 250 ms stops the script; batch world calls with world.batch.

## Things that are not limits but look like them
- Angles are degrees in the text language (a plain number is degrees); some parameter descriptions still say radians, which is how they are stored. Entity headings in game scripts are radians.
- Quality "preview" builds fields twice as coarse as "final"; a scene that fits in preview can still hit a budget in final.
- A texture or a program that fails to bake is a warning in evaluation.warnings, not a failure: look there when something renders flat.
- The studio hides its room when a game sets a camera; a scene without a game camera is looked at inside the studio room.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Read once with topics and operators together. Omit topics for core and menu; topic selects one, all returns everything.

tools.name: list_operators
tools.description: Search the operator and kit index; ids requests full specs or kit source. See get_guide(topic="operator_reference").

tools.name: texture_nodes
tools.description: Search the procedural texture node catalog with query, or describe one exact node with node. Use this before authoring a solid.texture@1 program.

tools.name: get_text
tools.description: The current document and revision as compact text by default, or canonical text with format="canonical".

tools.name: get_nodes
tools.description: Every node with its id, label, operator, parameters, inputs, flags, the group it belongs to (nodes inside a group definition) or its instance data, plus the outputs and the groups. Use the ids in apply_commands.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Revision, node count, evaluation state (last failure, timings) and the last projected geometry.

tools.name: survey
tools.description: Plan cameras and reachable surface coverage. See get_guide(topic="survey").

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Measure evaluated parts; summary by default, full JSON on request. See get_guide(topic="measure_reference").

tools.name: bake
tools.description: Bake a high-poly part's normals and ambient occlusion onto a low-poly part's UVs; the model must have unwrapped the low part with poly.unwrap_uv.

tools.name: apply_text
tools.description: Atomically add a text program and evaluate it, returning diagnostics and a state delta. dry_run applies, measures and undoes. See get_guide(topic="apply_text_reference") for limits and delta fields.

tools.name: scene_overview
tools.description: Scene parts, totals, bounds, evaluation time, warnings and provisional Quest budget. detail="full" lists every part.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Find document nodes by query, family, or one label/id with its inputs and users. See get_guide(topic="find_reference").

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Why did this node give this? Without node: every node in run order with what it made. With node (a label or id): its operator and parameters, what fed it, what it produced (kind, size, counts), what it changed from its main input, and the chain of nodes upstream, nearest first. Use it when a size, a count or a selection is not what you expected.

tools.name: check
tools.description: Looks for problems you can repair and answers each as {id, severity, message, node, fix}: a failed evaluation, the provisional Quest budget (over or near), operator warnings, and game kinds that name a scene part that does not exist. ok is false when any error is found. Run it after a build and before you call the work done; apply the fix, then run it again.

tools.name: game_describe
tools.description: The game the document defines (nodes game.var, game.kind, game.spawn, game.input, game.rule, game.goal joined by game.collect and output as `output rules = ...`): a one-line summary, its rules as text, and what validation found. Says how to build one when there is none.

tools.name: playtest
tools.description: Play headless with a deterministic policy and seed; aim:<thing tag>:<target tag>[,<target tag>...] swings a hand-held tool live toward targets. See get_guide(topic="playtest_reference").

tools.name: make_character
tools.description: Add an animated character from a body plan and sliders or custom creature. See get_guide(topic="character_reference") for every field.

tools.name: apply_commands
tools.description: Atomically apply typed commands by node id or unique label, returning a state delta. dry_run measures and undoes. See get_guide(topic="command_reference").

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Atomically edit nodes by unique label; returns the apply_text delta. Ops: set {node,params}, rename {node,to}, delete {node}, replace {node,text} (one replacement node line). See get_guide(topic="edit_diff").

tools.name: diff
tools.description: Compact added/changed/removed node lines since a revision (default previous revision); at most 80 lines, with an omitted count. See get_guide(topic="edit_diff").

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undoes the last committed edit.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redoes the last undone edit.

tools.name: world
tools.description: Reads and changes the running world by component name, beyond what document nodes can do. Pass method and params; see get_guide(topic="world_api") for all methods and their parameters.

tools.name: script
tools.description: Start, stop, list or read logs of JavaScript behaviour in the running world. See get_guide(topic="script_api") for the full API and execution limits.

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: Capture cameras, views, motion or a survey tour. See get_guide(topic="snapshot_modes").

tools.name: frame_view
tools.description: Moves the editor camera so the whole model fills the view, from a three-quarter angle. Call it after building something so the person watching sees it.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Moves the editor camera: position and target as [x, y, z] metres, so the person watching can see the result.
